newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes wind out of May at steady prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes wind out of May at steady prices.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes wound down May business Friday at mostly steady differentials, looking ahead to June barrels for next week, traders said.
Pipeline scheduling day has left domestic prices steady for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James and West Texas Sour/Midland, with May Postings also hovering at unchanged.
The May/June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing spread, or roll, was last done at minus 15 and 17 cents. May WTI was pegged at $19.95-$20.05 a barrel, 15 cts higher than Thursday.
Outright June prices have slipped on profit-taking, retracing late Thursday gains when bullish news was discarded.
